size: 142 gold queries: 112 development (80 run, 1,031 pairs) and 30 held out (23 run, 311 pairs)
score: dev: 397 rewrites (equivalent by construction), 0 refuted, 111 proved by the static layers; 634 mutations, 123 refuted with a stored witness, 167 differences withheld by the trust guard. Held-out: 127 rewrites, 0 refuted, 57 proved; 184 mutations, 25 refuted, 58 withheld
command: python tools/spider2_pairs.py --split dev --workers 4 (then --split held-out, run once)
caveats: Schemas are inferred from each query's own use of its tables (the public tables are not reachable), so the data are synthetic and a column type that runs is a guess. 32 dev and 7 held-out queries do not run (geography functions the emulator lacks, schema guesses it rejects). 31 of the 80 runnable dev queries and 10 of the 23 held-out ones return no rows on any of 20 random databases, so the 170 dev and 59 held-out rewrites on them agree trivially; 'proved' counts static proofs of all rewrites, vacuous ones included (dev 37 of 111, held-out 21 of 57). A rewrite is labelled equivalent by construction, not proved by anything but the static layers. Mutations are labelled not_equivalent only when the emulator finds a database where they differ and the trust guard allows it; an unlabelled mutation may or may not be equivalent. No proof of a refuted pair (0 false proofs). Held-out exposure: bq001 (first 1,500 characters) and bq004 (whole query) were read while debugging; both stay in the held-out file. Rewrite rules, mutation operators and the data generator were developed on the dev split only.
